mil3.4.8:0.3: 8. The Question on Extinguishment and Cessation
mil3.4.8:1.2: “Sir Nagasena, is cessation the same as extinguishment”?
mil3.4.8:1.5: “All the foolish common people, Great King, rejoice in, hold to, and cling to the inner and outer sense fields; they are swept along by that stream, and they do not escape from birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, sadness and despair. I say of them: ‘they do not escape from suffering’.
mil3.4.8:1.6: But a learned noble disciple, Great King, does not rejoice in, hold to, or cling to the inner and outer sense fields. Craving comes to rest in him who does not rejoice in, hold to, or cling to them; from the cessation of craving comes the cessation of clinging, from the cessation of clinging the cessation of becoming, from the cessation of becoming the cessation of birth, and from the cessation of birth old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, sadness and despair come to rest. Thus, for him, comes the cessation of the whole aggregate of suffering. Thus, Great King, cessation is extinguishment”.
